public.title: Minimum Spanning Tree Cost
public.description: Given an undirected weighted graph with n vertices labeled 0 through n-1 and edges of the form [u, v, weight], return the minimum total weight of a spanning tree. A spanning tree connects every vertex using n-1 edges and contains no cycle. Return -1 if no spanning tree exists. Define the answer as 0 when n is 0 or 1. Return only the cost: equally cheap spanning trees all yield the same answer, so no edge tie-breaking rule is needed. Constraints: n is an integer from 0 to 200; edges has 0 to 1000 triples of valid vertex labels (and must be empty when n = 0); each weight is an integer from 0 to 1000000. Self-loops and parallel edges, including reversed duplicates, are allowed. A self-loop cannot belong to a tree. Each parallel entry is a separate candidate edge. Edge input order has no effect on the answer. All possible costs are safe integers. Aim for O(m log(m + 1) + n) time, where m is the number of edge entries.
hints: Consider edges from cheapest to most expensive.
Use disjoint sets to detect whether an edge would create a cycle.
A minimum forest is not a spanning tree if some vertices remain disconnected.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and solutions, 2026. Uses standard graph algorithms; no third-party exercise text used.

explanation: Kruskal's algorithm sorts candidate edges by weight and adds an edge precisely when it joins different disjoint sets. The cut property permits each such cheapest connecting edge in some minimum spanning tree. Self-loops and cycle-forming edges are skipped. Union by size and path compression maintain the sets. After processing, n-1 accepted edges certify connectivity; otherwise return -1. For n at most 1 return the defined zero cost. With m edge entries, sorting and disjoint-set work take O(m log(m + 1) + n) time and O(n + m) auxiliary space including the copied sorted edges. The total is at most 199000000 in the supported domain. Functional tests check costs rather than proving complexity.
